groups.description: One front-view physical oscilloscope, occupying almost the entire image. One tall approximately rectangular outer case, one arch-shaped carrying handle above it, and two dark handle attachment feet. One large circular CRT assembly in the upper half, with an outer dark annular bezel and an inner circular rim. Four dark roughly rectangular mounting patches are visible around the screen at upper-left, upper-right, lower-left and lower-right.

The circular face contains an approximately rectilinear ruled lattice and one thick pale sinusoidal-looking trace progressing left-to-right. Three high lobes and two low lobes are visible, with partial ends rather than a separately marked cycle. Vertical and horizontal ruled lines are mixed with heavy scan/hatching artifacts. The circular aperture clips the lattice and trace. There are no readable numbers, units, axis names, or explicitly marked scale ticks.
uncertainties: Exact lattice row, column and line counts cannot be resolved independently from this degraded PNG because hatching and ruled marks merge. No exact count or numeric calibration is asserted.
The visible waveform endpoints and amplitudes are not calibrated; the rightmost high lobe is close to the aperture boundary.
The two concentric contour systems are visually separable, but their mechanical construction is not recoverable from the scan.

groups.description: One dark round control or socket is visible on the lower-right case. Two long thick hatched flexible leads run diagonally toward the lower-right border. Each has one visible rounded connector-like head at its upper-left end: one near the lower-left panel and one near the lower-middle bottom. The two other endpoints overlap or exit at the lower-right border. They are not visibly connected to a drawn outlet, live source, circuit or marked terminal.
uncertainties: The right-hand circular feature cannot be distinguished confidently as a knob versus socket.
The connector functions and hidden/border-overlapping destinations are not identifiable; no wiring procedure is implied.
